title: Spring timing gave no clear added summer flow forecast gain at the Lena gauge in 34 certified test years from 1980 to 2021
abstract: We tested whether April-June flow timing improves a June 30 forecast of August-September mean flow at Lena-Kyusyur. We used ArcticGRO v20261104 and fitted each forecast with earlier certified seasonal records from 1936. The reference used April-June mean flow and the mean summer flow in the previous five retained years. Adding the date of 50% cumulative April-June flow gave -0.09% mean squared error reduction in 34 test years. A conditional 95% five-year block range for error reduction was -4.86% to +3.26%. Root mean squared error changed from 6322.76 to 6325.62 cubic metres per second. All planned check ranges included zero. This extends earlier spring-volume and Canadian timing tests with a different input, target and lead at a large Siberian gauge. It gives no clear added gain for the tested linear model. It does not exclude physical effects of melt timing. Final revised records, retrospective certification, sparse later years, regulation, a short test and conditional uncertainty limit the result. Code, source hashes, aggregate results, a figure and an independent arithmetic audit support reproduction. External raw records and annual tables stay outside the package.
